name: Renfield Shake Motor
description: 12V shake motor - 'the signature', Renfield's tremble. BTS7960 H-bridge, operator-confirmed wiring 2026-09-26: RPWM = BCM GPIO 12, LPWM = BCM GPIO 13, R_EN and L_EN tied to 5 V (always enabled - no enable pins in software; leave renPin/lenPin absent). Driven by linear_actuator_control_v2.py (lgpio, works on this Pi 5): 'forward' puts PWM on GPIO 12, 'reverse' on GPIO 13. The 12 V motor supply is separate from the Pi; common ground on the logic side only. HISTORY: specced as a BTS7960 on 27/22/17/23 (never built), recorded as a Cytron MDD on DIR 26 / PWM 13 on 2026-09-13, and frozen by the 2026-09-20 lock as a disabled BTS7960 on 12/13. On 2026-09-26 the operator confirmed the BTS7960 on 12/13 with hard-wired enables; GPIO 26 belongs to the Writing Pen (part 7). STALL: a wiper-class motor stalls at roughly 24-40 A; short bursts only - scenes run 900-2000 ms at 50-80 %, maxDuration caps any single energization at 5000 ms. PWM outlives the process: killInFlightDrive() ends an overlapping drive before starting another.

name: Renfield Eye Rings
description:
Two chained DIYMall X0040MB5LN 8-bit WS2812B rings on GPIO18 - left eye pixels 0-7, right eye 8-15. Same hardware and same wiring as PumpkinHead's Pumpkin Eyes.

This part was registered as a plain switched `light` until 2026-09-20, which is why Renfield could toggle his eyes on and off and had no speech sync, no AI interaction colours and nothing on /setup/led-animation: every one of those paths selects parts by `type === 'led_ring'` and a `light` is invisible to all of them.

The old description claimed the rings were NOT addressable because rpi_ws281x cannot drive pixels on a Pi 5. The premise was right and the conclusion was wrong: rpi_ws281x fails because RP1 moved GPIO off the SoC, but RP1's own PIO block clocks WS2812B fine and needs no root (/dev/pio0 is root:gpio, and the service user is in the gpio group). led_ring_daemon.py picks that backend automatically on a Pi 5. Measured here: 500 frames at a steady 50 Hz with flat RSS.

GPIO18 is free on this node - the motor holds 12 and 13. It is also the Pi's I2S PCM_CLK line, unused because Renfield's audio is entirely USB (ReSpeaker XVF3800); move these rings first if I2S is ever enabled here. The PWM0/snd_bcm2835 contention that matters on a Pi 4 does not apply on this board, because the PIO path never touches PWM0.

name: PIR Motion Sensor
description: PIR motion sensor on BCM GPIO 22 (operator-stated wiring, 2026-09-26; first recorded as GPIO 16 the same evening, corrected by the operator). Output goes HIGH on motion; read with an internal pull-down (lgpio on this Pi 5 — no /dev/gpiomem). Arms the Motion toggle: detection -> AI + eye rings + shake + pen.

name: Writing Pen
description: Miuzei MG90S 180-degree micro servo that moves Renfield's writing pen. Driven DIRECTLY from BCM GPIO 20 = physical pin 38 (operator-stated 2026-09-26 late: orange pin 38, red pin 4 = 5 V, brown pin 39 = GND; it was on GPIO 26 then 21 earlier that evening) with lgpio tx_servo through servo_cli.py move_to — there is no PCA9685 on this Pi 5. Pulse 500-2400 us, 50 Hz. Servo power must come from a 5-6 V rail with a common ground to the Pi, never the Pi's 3.3 V. 2026-09-26 23:30 FINDING (software proven correct; the PIN is loaded): every driver — lgpio tx_servo, the kernel pwm-gpio driver, a bit-bang — puts the right command on GPIO 20, but the pad takes ~1040 us to rise and ~975 us to fall (free pins ~15 us) and reads LOW under the internal pull-up for 2 s. Measured at the pad with `pinctrl poll 20`: a 1450 us pulse arrives as ~770 us, 1133 us as ~100 us, 500 us never reaches a valid level, so the servo sits at one end whatever angle is asked. Symmetric ~1 ms edges plus a DC sink = a capacitor-class load, the signature of a servo SUPPLY lead (bulk cap + controller draw) on the pin, not a signal input; a dead pad or a missing ground fit the data worse. TOP SUSPECT: the red lead is on pin 38 (red/orange swapped, or the row counted from the wrong end). MORNING: (1) look at pin 38 — it must carry the signal lead; red on 2/4, brown on GND (39). (2) If orange really is on 38, pull it and run `python3 python_wrappers/servo_cli.py probe 20` bare: healthy (riseUs ~15) = the load comes through that lead, check its servo end; still LOADED bare = move the signal lead to physical pin 40 (GPIO 21, probed healthy; the pen moved on it earlier) and set pin 21 here. (3) probe healthy, then move_to <gpio> 1450 1000 to centre. Not yet calibrated: run Set Min/Max on /setup/calibration once probe reads healthy; the slider status now shows a WARNING whenever the line is loaded.
